title: Pay finite-bit walk errors while retaining the unresolved dynamic geometry cost
statement: For a prescribed T-step walk, uniformly bounded conditional per-choice TV errors delta_t couple the complete approximate and ideal paths with total TV<=sum_t delta_t; choosing O(epsilon/T) error per choice pays finite precision/capped randomness up to logarithmic factors rather than an exact-real or unbounded-rejection oracle. For a paired circle interval I, crossing pairs equal |I|-2*(number of wholly internal pairs), but dynamically changing order does not grant constant-time access. The cited chunk backend has(s+M/s)log M step cost and s+M/s>=2sqrt M. This is a lower bound on THAT representation and leaves a faster unrestricted backend open; finite-bit accounting alone does not remove its geometry cost.
